title: Apple Mail data
whyItMatters: Mail keeps local copies of messages, attachments and account settings. A new owner could read correspondence that was never deleted.
source: macforensics.app cheat sheet (Apple Mail); Apple lists ~/Library/Mail among folders that need Full Disk Access
notes: TCC-protected: without Full Disk Access the folder returns 'Operation not permitted' on a live system. Mailboxes are counted, never read.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Mail select the mailboxes to keep and use Mailbox > Export Mailbox to save them to a folder you keep.
cleanup.signOut: In Mail open Settings > Accounts and remove each account, so this Mac no longer signs in to them.
steps: Quit Mail so the mailbox files are not in use.
Delete the Mail folder named in the plan, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Local copies of messages and attachments are gone. Mail still on the provider's servers can be downloaded elsewhere.
